## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `XmlProcessing`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `xml`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **XmlProcessing**.

## Step 2: XML literals and construction

1. **Add a Variable**: In the flow designer, click **+** and select **Declare Variable**. Set the variable type to `xml` and provide an XML backtick template as the expression (for example: **xml `‹example›‹/example›`**).
2. <!-- manual: Add a Variable: In the flow designer, click + and select Declare Variable. Set the variable type to xml and provide an XML backtick template as the expression (for example: xml ‹example›‹/example›). -->
3. <!-- manual: Use embedded expressions: Insert dynamic values into XML templates using ${variableName} syntax. Each XML variable is represented as a separate Declare Variable step in the flow, allowing you to visually manage XML construction. -->
4. <!-- manual: Configure the expression: Select a variable node to view and edit the XML template expression from the side panel. -->

## Step 3: XML text and comments

1. <!-- manual: Add Variable: In the flow designer, add separate Declare Variable with the type set to xml for each XML node type such as text, comment, or processing instruction. -->

## Step 4: Navigating XML

1. **Define the XML input**: In the flow designer, click **+** and select **Declare Variable**. Set the type to `xml` and enter the XML literal as the expression. Name the variable `catalog`. This variable is then referenced in all subsequent navigation steps.
2. <!-- manual: Define the XML input: In the flow designer; enter the XML literal as the expression -->
3. <!-- manual: Navigate child elements: Add a Declare Variable step and use expressions such as catalog/‹product› to select child elements by name, or catalog/ to retrieve all child elements. -->
4. <!-- manual: Access text content: Use the .data() function in a variable expression (for example, (firstProduct/‹name›).data()) to extract the text value of an XML element. -->
5. <!-- manual: Access attributes: Use .getAttributes()["attributeName"] to retrieve attribute values from an XML element. -->
6. <!-- manual: Filter descendants: Use descendant navigation expressions such as catalog//‹name› to find matching elements at any level of the XML hierarchy. -->
7. <!-- manual: View and edit expressions: Select a variable node to view or modify the XML navigation expression from the side panel. -->

## Step 5: XML namespaces

1. <!-- manual: Add namespace declarations in code: Open the .bal file and declare the required namespaces (for example, xmlns "http://example.com/orders" as ord;). -->
2. <!-- manual: Navigate namespaced elements: Add a Declare Variable and use the namespace prefix in the expression (for example, nsOrder/‹cmn:customer›). -->
